title: The Captain Who Vanished on Lake Michigan, 1937

sources.what: 'Capt. George Doner', 'steamship O. S. McFarland', 'steaming to this port from Sheboygan Wednesday night', 'a cruise from Erie, Pa.'; sheriff, deputies, fishermen and Coast Guard searched; the report does not mention a locked door
sources.who: AP dispatch, Milwaukee Journal, Apr. 30, 1937 (reproduced by Strange Company)

sources.what: 'picked up 9,800 tons of coal in Erie, Penn.'; 'retired to his cabin, with the instructions that he be called'; 'the captain was not there'; 'while the ship was under way on April 28, 1937'; 'No clue as to what happened to Donner was ever found'; the locked door only as a 'reportedly' aside
O.S. McFarland: steel Great Lakes bulk freighter, built Toledo 1903
sources.who: Great Lakes Vessel History; BGSU Historical Collections of the Great Lakes

beats.text: A ship's captain vanished from his own ship on Lake Michigan. He was never seen again.
beats.label: LAKE MICHIGAN, 1937

beats.text: It was the night of April 28, 1937. Captain George Doner was bringing the freighter McFarland from Erie, Pennsylvania, to Port Washington, Wisconsin.
beats.label: THE O.S. McFARLAND, APRIL 28, 1937

beats.text: Later accounts say he went to his cabin to rest, and asked to be called when the ship neared port.
beats.label: THE CABIN

beats.text: They say that when a crewman went to wake him, the captain was not there.
beats.label: NOT THERE

beats.text: No sign of him was ever found.
beats.label: NEVER FOUND

beats.text: Some versions say his cabin door was locked from the inside. The 1937 Associated Press report doesn't mention it.
beats.label: THE LOCKED DOOR?

beats.text: Today it's told as part of the Lake Michigan Triangle. One account of the 1937 coverage says his crew believed he fell overboard. No one knows for sure.
beats.label: THE LAKE MICHIGAN TRIANGLE
